# Credential Management

Covers dimension 5. Sources referenced in [citations.md](../citations.md).

---

## Encryption

| Property | Value | Source |
|----------|-------|--------|
| Encryption key size | 256-bit | [14] |
| Key format | 32 hex characters (AP_ENCRYPTION_KEY) | [11] |
| Key generation | `openssl rand -hex 16` | [11] |
| Algorithm | Not specified in docs | — |
| At-rest encryption | Implied but not explicitly stated | [14] |

Credentials are stored with 256-bit encryption keys [14]. The encryption key is
configured via `AP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` environment variable (32 hexadecimal
characters / 16 bytes) [11]. A missing or malformed key causes an immediate
crash (Agent C discovery).

**Gap:** The specific encryption algorithm (AES-256-GCM, AES-256-CBC, etc.) is
not documented in the security practices page [14].

---

## API Isolation

The credential management model enforces strict separation between API callers
and stored credentials [14][17]:

1. **No retrieval API exists** — users cannot read stored credential values via
   the API [14]
2. **Execution-time only** — credentials are "sent only during processing, after
   which access is revoked from the engine" [14]
3. **Data masking** — "third-party credentials or any sensitive information are
   systematically censored within the logs" [14]

This means an API user (including the PA/LLM) can trigger workflows by ID or
webhook without ever accessing the credentials those workflows use. The engine
receives credentials only during execution and loses access afterward [14].

### Predefined Connections

For embedded/platform use, connections can be created at the platform level and
scoped to projects [17]:

- Created via Platform Admin → Security → API Keys [17]
- Stored encrypted and linked to projects via `projectIds` array [17]
- Support multiple auth types: PLATFORM_OAUTH2, SECRET_TEXT, BASIC_AUTH,
  CUSTOM_AUTH [17]
- Pieces retrieve connections via `ConnectionsManager.get()` using naming
  conventions [17]
- UI dropdown can be hidden (`requireAuth: false`) for seamless operation [17]

## OAuth2

Third-party integrations exclusively use OAuth2 authentication with minimized
scope requests "when third-party support allows" [14].

---

## Access Control

| Feature | Availability | Source |
|---------|-------------|--------|
| RBAC | Platform/Enterprise | [14] |
| SSO | Platform/Enterprise | [14] |
| Audit logging | Platform/Enterprise | [14] |
| API keys | Platform/Enterprise | [15] |
| Password hashing | All editions | [14] |

API keys for programmatic access are available in Platform and Enterprise
editions only [15]. This is a potential limitation for the personal assistant use
case — the community edition may not have API key generation for REST API access.

---

## Assessment for Personal Assistant Use Case

**Meets the core requirement.** The PA (LLM) triggers workflows by webhook or
API without accessing credentials. The engine handles credentials internally
during execution and revokes access afterward [14].

**Concern:** API key availability. The REST API requires API keys generated from
Platform Admin → Security [15][17], which may be a Platform/Enterprise feature
not available in the community edition. Webhooks remain available in all editions
as an alternative trigger mechanism.
